summary: Retest of iteration_14 security fixes. Backend: 13/13 pass in test_iteration15_throttle_csrf.py. Login throttle: a throwaway email gets five 401s, then 429 on the 6th attempt. The ip identifier is now the real client IP (35.x), not the pod IP. CSRF: logout with Origin evil.example -> 403 and the session stays valid. Referer evil.example with no Origin -> 403. Origin 'null' -> 403. Look-alike origin (<app>.evil.example) -> 403. Form-urlencoded empty-body POST /api/saved/programs/{id} with evil Origin -> 403 and nothing is written to the DB. Content-Type 'Application/JSON' with the app's own Origin -> 200 (not 415). A same-origin Referer is allowed. Own-origin logout -> 200. GET with an evil Origin is not blocked. Cron with Bearer secret and no Origin -> 200 (wrong secret -> 401). Frontend regression: UI login -> /dashboard; saved-job status PATCH interviewed->applied->interviewed (200, 200); /jobs live-job save/unsave (POST 200, DELETE 200); logout -> /auth/me 401. No same-origin browser request was blocked (403/415). One residual weakness: X-Forwarded-For can be spoofed (see below).

minor.issue: _client_ip trusts the FIRST X-Forwarded-For hop, which the client controls. The ingress appends to a client-supplied XFF instead of overwriting it. Verified: 8 failed logins for one email, each with a different spoofed X-Forwarded-For (1.2.3.0-7), all returned 401 and none 429. Each got its own '1.2.3.N:email' identifier. The 5-attempt ip+email limit can be bypassed; only the acct:email limit (20 per 15 min) still caps an attacker. Fix: use the right-most entry, or right-most minus the number of trusted proxies (the hop added by the trusted ingress), or X-Real-IP if the ingress sets it from the socket and overwrites it.

action_items: Optional hardening: in _client_ip, use the right-most (trusted-proxy-appended) X-Forwarded-For entry instead of the first one, so spoofed XFF headers can't rotate past the 5-attempt ip+email throttle
critical_code_review_comments: _client_ip: first-hop X-Forwarded-For can be spoofed (see minor issue).

csrf_and_headers: the 415 check only runs when Content-Length is non-zero. A chunked request (Transfer-Encoding without Content-Length) with a non-JSON body skips it. Low risk because the Origin check now runs first, but consider also checking for transfer-encoding.
Requests with no Origin and no Referer are allowed. This is fine for non-browser clients, and modern browsers always send Origin on cross-site POSTs.
server.py is ~1350 lines and should be split into routers (auth, jobs, ai, cron, middleware).

success_rate.backend: 100% (13/13); XFF spoof bypass found by an extra probe
